# Running the Machine {.unnumbered}

\lettrine{B}{uilding} a physical AI machine is fundamentally an exercise in **reconciling disparate timescales, representations, and failure domains**.

No single algorithm, neural model, or silicon core can span the vast continuum between high-level human reasoning and low-level physical dynamics. At the deliberative tier, human intent and task semantics are linguistic and symbolic, evolving over seconds ($0.1\text{--}1\text{ Hz}$). In the middle tier, physical space is continuous and metric, requiring 3D spatial representations and smooth kinematic trajectories generated at tens of hertz ($20\text{--}50\text{ Hz}$). At the execution tier, motor torque control is electromagnetic and immediate, demanding cycle-deterministic execution at kilohertz frequencies ($1000\text{ Hz}$) on bare-metal silicon to prevent mechanical resonance and kinetic destruction.

::: {#pri-multi-rate-separation .callout-principle title="The Multi-Rate Separation Theorem"}

**Invariant**: An embodied physical machine must decouple its operational cadences across three distinct, non-interfering temporal regimes:
$$ \text{Deliberation } (0.1\text{--}5\text{ Hz}) \;\ll\; \text{Kinematic Tracking } (20\text{--}50\text{ Hz}) \;\ll\; \text{Impedance/Safety } (1000\text{ Hz}) $$
Directly coupling these tiers into a monolithic loop forces an impossible dilemma: either the fast inner loop misses deadlines waiting for neural inference, or high-capacity foundation models are artificially starved of computation.

**Implication**: The runtime software architecture must enforce structural decoupling using asynchronous, lock-free double-buffered shared memory structures. Each tier must execute independently at its natural physical cadence without blocking on slower upstream layers.

:::

Spatial perception in an embodied machine is dynamic: moving cameras observe moving objects, meaning observation validity decays with elapsed time.

::: {#pri-information-freshness .callout-principle title="The Information-Age Invariant"}

**Invariant**: A physical sensor observation's spatial uncertainty expands dynamically with elapsed sensor age $\tau_{\text{age}} = t_{\text{curr}} - t_{\text{capture}}$ under relative plant and object velocity $v_{\text{rel}}$:
$$ \Delta x_{\text{uncertainty}} \approx v_{\text{rel}} \cdot \tau_{\text{age}} + \frac{1}{2} a_{\text{rel}} \cdot \tau_{\text{age}}^2 $$
A 100-millisecond-old detection for a robot moving at $1.5\text{ m/s}$ creates an immediate $15\text{ cm}$ spatial error—violating precision manipulation tolerances.

**Implication**: Sensor data without hardware timestamping is invalid. Ingestion pipelines must bind sensor age at the SerDes DMA controller, compensate for rolling shutter line delays, and enforce explicit temporal decay rates on spatial memory transforms to prevent "frozen transform" collisions.

:::

When the high-capacity neural deliberative model experiences latency jitter, GPU thermal throttling, or out-of-distribution confusion, the physical machine cannot simply freeze or pause time.

::: {#pri-simplex-veto .callout-principle title="The Simplex Separation Invariant"}

**Invariant**: Let $\mathcal{C} = \{x \in \mathbb{R}^n \mid h(x) \ge 0\}$ define a safe forward-invariant set under Control Barrier Function $h(x)$. If the advanced neural controller fails to deliver an action before deadline $t > t_{\text{deadline}}$ or proposes an action that breaches $\dot{h}(x, u) + \alpha(h(x)) < 0$, the system deterministically switches to an unoptimizing, formally certified baseline controller:
$$ u(t) = \begin{cases} u_{\text{advanced}}(t) & \text{if } t \le t_{\text{deadline}} \text{ and } \dot{h}(x, u_{\text{adv}}) + \alpha(h(x)) \ge 0 \\ u_{\text{baseline}}(x) & \text{otherwise} \end{cases} $$

**Implication**: Neural software exceptions, memory stalls, or out-of-distribution hallucinations cannot compromise physical safety. The baseline safety controller must execute on physically isolated hardware cores with zero software dependencies on the neural stack.

:::

Part III details **The Living Organism: The Millisecond Pipeline** that transforms raw physical sensor photons into coordinated motor currents:

* **From Photons to Spatial Claims (@sec-perception):** How raw, uncompressed sensor streams from SerDes lanes are ingested via DMA ring buffers, corrected for rolling-shutter distortion, calibrated against IMUs, and lifted into calibrated metric $SE(3)$ spatial claims under strict information-age budgets.
* **Preserving Belief Under Occlusion (@sec-memory):** How spatial representations (transform trees, TSDF voxel grids, 3D Gaussian Splats) persist when objects pass behind obstacles or cameras pan away, enforcing explicit temporal decay rates to prevent "frozen transform" collisions.
* **From Semantic Goals to Reachable Affordances (@sec-intent):** How open-vocabulary foundation models decompose human language into spatial affordances, issuing cryptographically bounded, expiring **Intent Leases** with hard time-to-live (TTL) envelopes that fail-safe on silence.
* **Synthesizing Continuous Motion (@sec-planning):** How continuous generative models predict $H$-step action chunks, smooth kinematic transitions across chunk boundaries using $C^2$ jerk splines, and guarantee safe stopping suffixes when upstream inference experiences latency spikes.
* **The Deterministic Gatekeeper (@sec-enforcement):** The bare-metal 1 kHz safety shield. We implement Control Barrier Functions (CBFs) and quadratic programming (QP) projection on dedicated microcontrollers, enforcing the Four-Tier Fallback Ladder and the Simplex Architecture Pattern to retain exclusive veto authority over power stages.
* **The Silicon Substrate (@sec-placement):** How high-throughput neural deliberation and hard-real-time safety co-exist on shared heterogeneous System-on-Chip (SoC) platforms. We quantify on-chip memory crossbar QoS, DRAM bank contention, power distribution network ($L \frac{dI}{dt}$) voltage droop, and hysteretic thermal clock throttling.

Part III teaches students how to architect, synchronize, and isolate the six computational stages that keep high-level machine intelligence grounded in physical reality.
